notes_for_editor: Revision pass on the earlier draft. The opening no longer states the 1933 end as settled: LighthouseFriends gives late September 1933 (a lighted bell buoy replaced it); the NRHP says decommissioned 1934. LighthouseFriends gives the official-service span as 1 Jan 1857 to August 1933 in one place and late September 1933 in another. LighthouseFriends quotations cut to short phrases (copyrighted-source limit). Owners after about 1960 are not named (the 1956 couple, the 1983 buyer, the 1995 owner and the 2004 buyer); Bernice Richmond is named only as the author of two books and as the 1939 owner, her connection having ended before 1960. The LighthouseFriends sentence on the 1934 auction calls the station 'Winter Island Lighthouse' (apparent typo); the $552 price in that sentence is also LighthouseFriends' figure for Pumpkin Island, so no price is given here. Gerrish to Wasgatt handover: roster 1860, LighthouseFriends 1861 (both stated). Adelbert C. Leighton's end: roster and LighthouseFriends keeper list 1924, LighthouseFriends narrative 1927 (both stated). Storm, wreck and rescue: none tied to this light in the Board volumes read (1891-1899 show minor repairs only), the Commissioner volume or the Bulletins 1921-28 in the corpus; the 1918 Mark Island rescue in the Commissioner volume is in West Penobscot Bay and is a different station. Mark Island name clashes excluded: the Deer Isle Thorofare light on Mark Island (Board 1895-96) and the Harpswell Mark Island (Bulletin 1936) are different stations. The shape uses five chapters, not the moderate two to four, because the sources include Board annual reports and a nomination; the text stays within the moderate word range. No newspaper search was run for this station in this pass (the earlier run found no Maine hits for 1933-34). Fact-check 2026-10-22 (second pass): units added to the story (19 ft = 6 m, 37 ft = 11 m, 15 ft = 4.6 m). The structure note previously credited the 19 ft height to the NRHP; the NRHP gives no tower height, so the note now cites the USLHS place record and LighthouseFriends. The USLHS place record gives 37 ft above mean high water, which agrees with LighthouseFriends' 37 ft focal plane. Board passages confirmed on scan 48, 374 (1891-92), 53 (1893-94) and 78 (1899). The 1856 opening claim now carries the NRHP footnote. Owners after about 1960 stay unnamed, and the story reports the 2004 sale without naming the buyer. The footnoted accessed dates (2026-10-23) post-date the 2026-10-22 check date and should be reconciled.
